summary.headline: Campus Activewear Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, EBITDA margin 19.2%, FY26 PAT margin 8.4%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, led by online (around 19%) and distribution (around 5.5%). EBITDA was INR 88.5 crore at a 19.2% margin (up 50 bps) and PAT was INR 44.1 crore at a 9.6% margin (up 100 bps). For FY26, revenue grew 11.4% to INR 1,774 crore, EBITDA margin rose 145 bps to 17.5%, and PAT margin rose 80 bps to 8.4%. Management said the mid-year raw material and minimum wage inflation was passed on via MRP hikes taken in early April, and that demand held up in April.

segments.name: Online (marketplace)
segments.commentary: Online grew about 19% in Q4 and 9.8% in FY26; management said all online business is pure marketplace except Flipkart, with Amazon, Snapdeal and brand.com growing faster. Online salience rose in Q4, though GT charges dilute gross margin and billing changed from 16 June to net of freight (INR 82 billed against INR 100 earlier).

segments.name: Distribution (general trade and franchise)
segments.commentary: Distribution grew about 5.5% in Q4 and 10.5% in FY26. Management said the annual distribution meet produced strong four-month forward orders, with AOP alignments with partners closed at over 100% of the target till September.

segments.name: Sneakers
segments.commentary: Sneaker portfolio grew about 100% YoY in FY26 and more than 50% in quarterly terms; the Paonta Sahib and Pant Nagar units are producing about 2 lakh pairs per month, targeted to double by end FY27. Management did not disclose sneaker revenue or volume share.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated its EBITDA margin aspiration band of 17% to 19% for FY27 but gave no formal FY27 margin guidance.
Management said pricing taken in early April covers the inflation impact and that raw material prices have peaked and are starting to ease; no further price hikes expected.
Plan to open 60 to 80 new EBO stores in FY27 (about 40% COCO and 60% FOFO), after closing 9 to 10 and opening 13 to 14 stores in FY26; store count stood at about 300.
Marketing budget for FY27 set to be aggressive, focused on brand building rather than performance marketing.

Capex in FY27 expected to return to normal maintenance, mold, EBO and IT levels; Pant Nagar expansion including assembly lines is planned over the next three years, after first optimising the upper facility.
Full BIS compliance expected by 31 July 2026, with very little BIS stock remaining.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share of shoes priced below INR 1,000 rise versus Q4 FY25, and is the pricing MRP or realised price?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the figures are realised ASP; the shift reflects MRP corrections after GST on footwear was revised from 12% to 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What size of price hike was taken and will it suffice against inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO declined to give the percentage, said hikes were taken proportionately across the range and are enough to cover raw material and minimum wage inflation; peak RM seen, prices to ease in about a quarter, with no price reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses (ex-ad spend) rise only about 5% despite online growth of 19%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited dynamic online commission negotiations and event-based waivers, plus flat store count meaning no new EBO costs; other costs grew in the 5-6% range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lease cash outflow rise sharply, nearly 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Pant Nagar land is a 71-year state government lease treated as lease liability payment; normalised FY26 rent excluding INR 65.4 crore is the base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise 5-6 days in FY26 and where will they go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FG inventory was at a very minimal level last year and was rebuilt to the right level by March 2026, which will be maintained going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity a constraint for sneaker growth, and what is the path to 2 lakh pairs a month?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said capacity is not a constraint now; Pant Nagar can reach 6 lakh pairs per month after two phases and HRD2 can reach 2 lakh (already running), targeting 8-9 lakh pairs per month in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins reach the 17-19% band or slip to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; CEO said the company will endeavour to stay within the 17-19% range guided earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBO expansion plan and capex for stores and facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said 60-70 or about 80 new stores are planned after closing 9-10 and opening 13-14 in FY26; CFO said FY27 capex reverts to normal maintenance, mould, EBO and IT levels, with Pant Nagar expansion over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What were the distribution meet outcomes and demand trend?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said order bookings were strong on a four-month forward basis, numbers not shared; COO said AOP alignments with distributors were closed at over 100% till September.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the low Q4 ASP growth of 1.5% when D2C/online realisations should be higher?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to online billing change from 16 June (INR 82 billed against INR 100) with freight of INR 18 billed directly by portals, which is not in last year's Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the BIS compliance position?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the company is hardly left with any non-BIS stock and expects full compliance by 31 July 2026; the reported BIS rethink is only chatter with no official communication.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company gaining share in competitive affordable athleisure, and what are its moats?
qa_highlights.answer: COO cited an integrated supply chain, strongest distribution network, R&D, 20-year brand loyalty; CEO estimated replicating the supply chain would need about INR 2,000 crore.

capex_capacity: Sneaker capacity: Paonta Sahib upper facility stabilised; Pant Nagar unit production commenced; combined output about 2 lakh pairs per month, targeted to double by end FY27.

Management targets 8-9 lakh pairs per month of sneaker production in totality; Pant Nagar can reach 6 lakh pairs per month after 2 development phases, HRD2 can reach 2 lakh pairs (already operating at that level).
Management said capacity is not a constraint at present, with capacity being added in phases.

FY27 capex to return to normal range: plant routine maintenance, mould, EBO store additions and IT infra; FY26 was elevated by the Pant Nagar acquisition. Pant Nagar expansion incl. assembly lines over next three years, after first optimising the upper facility at Pant Nagar.

Plan to open 60-80 EBO stores in FY27 (CFO/CEO gave varying figures: 60-70 or about 80 in one answer; 30-35 stores with capex), with COCO capex only for company-operated stores (about 40% COCO, 60% FOFO).
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 ASP INR 668 per pair (+1.5% YoY); FY26 ASP INR 683 (+7% from INR 658), driven by sneakers and women/kids mix.
Online grew about 19% in Q4 and 9.8% in FY26; distribution grew about 5.5% in Q4 and 10.5% in FY26.
Q4 ASP dilution attributed to online billing change from 16 June: billing INR 82 against INR 100 earlier, with INR 18 freight billed directly by portals; also school shoe mix in Q4.

Price hikes taken early April 2026 across the range, passed on raw material (EVA, PU) and minimum wage inflation; management said it would not disclose the size; said pricing covers inflation and no further hikes expected.
Management said raw material prices have peaked and are easing; latest purchase at slightly lower prices. Demand impact visible only marginally in March; April started positively.
Distribution meet: four-month forward orders described as strong, numbers not shared; AOP alignments with distributors closed at over 100% of target till September (after excluding April revenue).
Men:women and children mix 78:22 in Q4 (vs 81:19); 79:21 for FY26 (vs 80:20). Gross margin 52.1% Q4 (vs 52.3%) and 53.5% FY26 (vs 52.3%).

Management estimated industry growth at 7-8% last year vs Campus about 12%, implying market share gains; sneaker portfolio grew about 100% in FY26 and 50%+ quarterly, though sneaker revenue share not disclosed.
Post-GST change (12% to 5%) MRP corrections shifted pairs between price bands, with more pairs now priced below INR 1,000.
risks_watch: Raw material and minimum wage inflation: management says peak is passed, but the war-linked supply situation is uncertain; if it persists, demand and margins could be hit.
Demand elasticity after April MRP hikes: management said resistance is expected, with Q1 FY27 demand still to be tested.
Online marketplace dependency: commissions, event waivers, GT charges and billing change (INR 82 vs INR 100) dilute ASP and gross margin.
Working capital: inventory days up 5-6 days in FY26 after FG rebuild; monitor whether it normalises.
EBO expansion of 60-80 stores in FY27 (after 9-10 closures and 13-14 openings in FY26) adds fixed costs and capex; store count at about 300 today.
Marketing budget and logo transition: brand-building spend is set to be aggressive, so the margin impact needs tracking.
key_quotes: We have taken enough increase in pricing to cover the inflationary impact.
I think we have seen the peak and with time, in maybe a quarter or so, it should start coming down as the war settles, but the pricing will not change.
So I would not say that capacity is a constraint at this point.
So, we will be fully compliant by 31st of July.
summary.management_tone: Confident on pricing power, sneaker capacity and market-share gains, with stated caution on the war-linked demand outlook and no formal FY27 margin guidance (only a reiterated 17-19% aspiration band). Management was evasive on the price-hike percentage, distribution order values and the number of new stores.

adds.what: Sneaker production at Paonta Sahib and Pant Nagar units, about 2 lakh pairs/month, targeted to double by end FY27
Pant Nagar sneaker expansion incl. assembly lines (can reach 6 lakh pairs/month after 2 development phases), planned over next three years
Company-run and franchise EBO stores: 60-80 planned in FY27 (about 40% COCO, 60% FOFO); 13-14 opened in FY26, store count about 300

growth.why: No formal FY27 revenue guidance; growth is supported by strong distribution forward orders (AOP over 100% of target till September), online salience, sneaker capacity of about 2 lakh pairs/month doubling by end FY27, and 60-80 EBO store openings, with EBITDA margin only reiterated at 17-19% and capacity said to be not a constraint.
